Launched 2023-12-06. AMD quotes dense figures separately from sparsity (sparse = 2x). 8 XCD chiplets on 4 IODs; 7 x 128 GB/s IF links in an 8-GPU platform.
Announced Computex 2024, launched 2024-10-10, volume Q1 2025. Same compute as MI300X with 256 GB HBM3E.
Air-cooled variant; CDNA 4; launched Advancing AI 2025 (2025-06-12), shipping Q3 2025. FP6 = FP4 rate. 7 x 153.6 GB/s IF links.
Liquid-cooled, higher-clock MI350X; racks of up to 128 GPUs are joined by Ethernet scale-out, not one scale-up domain. Dense figures.

MI400-series flagship for the 72-GPU Helios rack (rack: 2.9 EF FP4, 1.4 EF FP8, 31 TB HBM4, 260 TB/s scale-up -> 3.6 TB/s per GPU). Per-GPU 40/20 PFLOPS and 432 GB/19.6 TB/s are AMD figures (June 2025); AMD has historically quoted dense rates but did not say here. 320B transistors and N2 are press-reported from CES 2026. H2 2026 availability (OpenAI 1 GW first tranche). Not re-verified this session. Sibling parts: MI430X (FP64/HPC), MI440X (8-GPU).
Previewed at CES 2026 for 2027 (CDNA next; annual cadence). No specs disclosed - cells blank. Not re-verified this session.
Deployed internally from 2020; Cloud GA 2022. 3D-torus ICI reconfigured by OCS; per-chip ICI bandwidth not recorded here.
Cost-optimised inference/training part. ICI 1,600 Gbps per chip converted to GB/s; Google does not state the direction basis.
Training flagship of 2023-24. ICI 4,800 Gbps per chip converted to GB/s (direction basis not stated).
Announced May 2024, GA Dec 2024. 4.7x v5e peak compute per chip. ICI 3,584 Gbps converted.

Announced 2025-04-09, GA Nov 2025; first TPU with native FP8; dual-chiplet. 9,216-chip superpod = 42.5 EF FP8. BF16 = half FP8 (reported, not in launch blog). TDP not disclosed. Google has begun offering TPUs beyond its own cloud (e.g., Anthropic up to 1M TPUs, reports of Meta purchases) - availability still mainly via Google Cloud. Not re-verified this session.
Trn1 GA Oct 2022; 16 chips per trn1.32xlarge.
Inf2 GA April 2023; 12 chips per inf2.48xlarge.
Announced re:Invent 2023, GA Dec 2024; Trn2 UltraServer = 64 chips. Project Rainier (Anthropic) built on Trn2. NeuronLink-v3 ~1.28 TB/s per chip (not re-verified).

GA at re:Invent 2025 (Dec 2025). Trn3 UltraServer: 144 chips, ~362 PFLOPS FP8, 20.7 TB HBM3E, 706 TB/s -> per chip 2.52 PFLOPS / 144 GB / 4.9 TB/s. BF16 and TDP not disclosed. Not re-verified this session.

Previewed at re:Invent 2025 with multipliers vs Trainium3: 6x FP4 compute, 4x memory bandwidth, 2x capacity. Memory cells are this repo's Est. (2 x 144 GB; 4 x 4.9 TB/s). FP4 left blank because the Trainium3 FP4 base rate is not public. Launch timing not given (2026-27).

Announced Ignite 2023; details at Hot Chips 2024. ~820 mm2 die; 500 W provisioned (700 W design). Peak dense ~3 POPS at 6-bit MX, ~0.8 PFLOPS BF16. 12 x 400 GbE = 4.8 Tb/s backend (direction basis unspecified). Limited internal deployment.

Announced Jan 2026 as an inference accelerator (Azure US Central first); Microsoft quoted >10 PFLOPS FP4 and >5 PFLOPS FP8 (lower bounds used), 272 MB on-chip SRAM, >140B transistors, 750 W SoC TDP; clusters up to 6,144 chips. Figures recalled, not re-verified this session.
Recommendation inference ASIC; bf16 column holds FP16. Off-chip LPDDR5 (not HBM).
256 MB on-chip SRAM; sparse figures (354 BF16 / 708 INT8) halved. Newer MTIA generations (incl. HBM-based parts, Rivos acquisition 2025) not captured: not verifiable this session.
BF16 matrix rate as commonly reported (Intel published FP8 865 TFLOPS). Ethernet doubles as scale-up (8 per node) and scale-out.
Two dies; launched Sept 2024; OAM 900 W (air). Intel cut 2024 Gaudi revenue goal and pivoted to a GPU roadmap.

Announced OCP 2025-10-14: Xe3P inference GPU, 160 GB LPDDR5X, air-cooled; customer sampling H2 2026. Rack-scale successor Jaguar Shores (after Falcon Shores was cancelled as a product in Jan 2025) not captured - no specs. Not re-verified this session.
Specs vary by SKU (FP16 ~280-376 TFLOPS reported); bf16 column holds FP16. No FP8. China-only availability.
Two 910B-class dies in one package; CloudMatrix 384 supernode (384 NPUs) from April 2025. bf16 column = FP16 800 TFLOPS from Huawei roadmap slide. No FP8.

As announced at Huawei Connect 2025 (2025-09-18) for Q1 2026: prefill/recommendation variant with low-cost in-house HBM. Supports FP8/MXFP8/HiF8 and MXFP4/HiF4 (dense vs sparse not stated). Atlas 950 SuperPoD = 8,192 chips (Q4 2026). Launch status not re-verified this session.
As announced at Huawei Connect 2025 for Q4 2026: decode/training variant with higher-bandwidth in-house HBM. Same compute die as 950PR.
As announced at Huawei Connect 2025 for Q4 2027; Atlas 960 SuperPoD = 15,488 chips.
As announced at Huawei Connect 2025 for Q4 2028 (some specs described as targets).
Cambricon does not publish an English spec sheet; capacity is press-reported and compute figures vary widely across reports (left blank). Successor (Siyuan 690) reported but unverified.

46,225 mm2 wafer-scale die; 900,000 cores. Cerebras quotes 125 PFLOPS peak AI compute with sparsity (dense basis not published, left blank). tdp_w is the CS-3 system (~23 kW, reported). Up to 2,048 CS-3 per cluster (vendor). Excluded from bubble charts (off-scale SRAM bandwidth).

bf16 column = FP16. Served via GroqCloud and GroqRack. Reconfigurable dataflow unit, 2 dies; 520 MB SRAM + 64 GB HBM + up to 1.5 TB DDR per socket. HBM bandwidth not stated in data. Corporate status (reported sale talks in late 2025) not verified this session.
RISC-V Tensix cores plus 16 SiFive X280 cores; Galaxy server = 32 Blackhole chips. Compute figures as reported by Tenstorrent marketing (basis not always stated).

Digital in-memory-compute inference card (announced 2024-11-19): 2 GB SRAM 'performance memory' at 150 TB/s plus 256 GB LPDDR5 'capacity memory'; 2,400 TFLOPS MXINT8 and 9,600 TFLOPS 4-bit block formats (not FP4, so fp4 blank). 600 W per card.
Transformer-only ASIC announced June 2024; vendor claims >500,000 tokens/s on Llama 70B per 8-chip server. No FLOPS, power or shipping evidence verified this session.
PCIe card built from four AI 100 SoCs; bf16 column holds FP16. 150 W card power is the key selling point (perf/W).

Announced 2025-10-27 for 2026: rack-scale inference card with 768 GB LPDDR per card (capacity/TCO focus), direct liquid cooling, 160 kW rack, confidential computing. HUMAIN (Saudi Arabia) 200 MW first customer. Compute and bandwidth not disclosed. Public information only.
Announced 2025-10-27 for 2027: near-memory computing architecture claimed to give >10x higher effective memory bandwidth at lower power than AI200. No absolute figures disclosed.

OpenAI-designed, Broadcom-developed accelerator: 10 GW of racks to deploy from H2 2026 to end-2029. No silicon specs public (press code names unverified). Broadcom also co-designs Google TPUs and Meta MTIA.
